tagline.text: Pine forest at 2,300 m and the site of the 1986 peace accord

location.label: Location
location.text: On the Benguet–Mountain Province border, along Halsema Highway

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–3,500 (from Baguio, per person, day trip to one hotel night)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), then overland via Baguio

children.text: Rising at about 2,300 m along Halsema Highway north of Baguio, this national park is a cool mountain stop of pine forest and mossy oak forest. It is also home to Mount Data Hotel, the setting of the 1986 peace accord, and makes a good rest stop on the way to Sagada or Banaue.
Mount Data is a peak of about

in the heart of the Cordillera range in northern Luzon, straddling the border of Benguet and Mountain Province. The mountain and its surroundings were declared a national park in 1936, and the park was expanded to about 5,513 hectares in 1940. Rather than a single summit to tick off, it works best as a halfway stop on Halsema Highway, which links Baguio with Sagada, Bontoc and Banaue, where you can enjoy cool air and pine forest.

The park holds the headwaters of several major rivers, including the Chico, Ahin, Siffu, Abra and Amburayan, and the Agno River also begins here. That makes it an important watershed supplying drinking and irrigation water to many towns in Mountain Province, Benguet and Ifugao. The slopes are covered with pine forest and mossy oak forest, and since the late 19th century British and American naturalists have collected and studied Luzon's endemic rodents and birds here, so the area is known for its biodiversity. Small mammals and endemic birds such as Whitehead's swiftlet have been recorded.

The most prominent facility for travelers is Mount Data Hotel, inside the park on the Bauko side. The Philippine Tourism Authority built it in the 1960s to promote tourism in the Cordillera. It closed in 2005 and, after a major renovation, reopened on May 5, 2022. On September 13, 1986, the Aquino government and the Cordillera People's Liberation Army (CPLA) signed a peace accord here that ended armed conflict and led to the creation of the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), which makes this a place of real significance in modern Philippine history.

The weather is cool all year and mornings can bring frost. Baguio is chilly, but here it is much colder. When it is clear, sunlight filters through the pines, and when clouds roll in, fog can cut visibility to a few meters in moments. It suits travelers who want to see the opposite of the glamorous beach Philippines, or who want to spend a day in the highlands on the way to Sagada or Banaue.

blocks.title: A walk in the pine forest at 2,300 m

children.text: The park is a highland forest of pines and mossy oaks. Strolling slowly along the paths and forest trails around the hotel, you will find a landscape completely unlike the tropical image most people have of the Philippines. On humid days the branches are heavy with moss and epiphytes.

blocks.title: Mount Data Hotel and the peace accord

children.text: The hotel where the 1986 peace accord was signed reopened in May 2022. It has 22 rooms and two 10-person dormitories, a restaurant and a coffee shop and bar, and its roughly 7.7-hectare grounds include pine forest and picnic areas. The lobby with its fireplace is a good place to warm up with a hot drink.

blocks.title: Source of the Agno and four other great rivers

children.text: The Chico, Ahin, Siffu, Abra and Amburayan rivers all branch off from these slopes. The Agno River also begins here, so you are seeing the starting point of the waters that feed rice fields and villages across the Cordillera. It is far more interesting with signs and a local guide to explain it.

Scientists have collected and studied mammals and birds here since the late 19th century. If you listen at the forest edge early in the morning, you may hear highland birds that are hard to find in the lowlands. Be sure to bring binoculars and warm clothing.

blocks.title: Gateway to the Bauko Seven Peaks trek

children.text: The Bauko area around the park is also known for a two-day trek linking seven peaks, including Mt. Polis. The usual starting point is the village of Bila in Bauko, and you need to hire a local guide and register at the barangay office. The trek is demanding, so beginners need preparation.

Mount Data lies on the stretch of Halsema Highway that runs from Baguio toward Bontoc. Winding mountain roads, cliffs, terraced vegetable farms and views above the clouds make the road itself a highlight. You can also stop at the highest-point viewpoint on Halsema Highway in nearby Atok (about 2,255 m).
With no city lights, clear nights show many stars, and on foggy mornings the pine forest looks mysterious. This is a pleasure only overnight guests get to enjoy.

items.title: Day stop from Baguio
items.subtitle: Ride up Halsema Highway and look around the forest and hotel

children.text: Board a Sagada- or Bontoc-bound bus or van at a terminal in Baguio. Mount Data is on this route, so tell the driver in advance that you are getting off in front of Mount Data Hotel.
You arrive in the Mount Data Hotel area. The trip takes about
3 hours
, but it varies a lot with road and weather conditions. Put on warm clothes as soon as you arrive.
Take a slow walk through the pine forest around the hotel and try the eco trail. Take photos in the hotel garden and picnic area.
Have lunch at the hotel restaurant and rest by the fireplace. Ask in advance whether local dishes are on the menu.
Check the time of the last ride toward Sagada or Baguio, then wait by the road. In the mountains, rides can stop running late in the afternoon, so allow plenty of time.
A day trip leaves little time on site because of the long travel. If you can, stay one night.

items.title: One-night highland retreat
items.subtitle: Stay at the hotel, then continue to Sagada or Bauko the next day

children.text: Leave Baguio, stop at the Halsema Highway highest-point viewpoint in Atok for photos, then reach Mount Data Hotel around lunchtime and unpack.
Forest walk and rest at the hotel. The temperature drops sharply at dusk, so come indoors early.
If it is clear, enjoy the misty forest at dawn and the birdsong. After breakfast, continue toward Sagada or Bontoc.
The times are examples. Check current bus departure times and road conditions locally.
From Manila (Pasay or Quezon City), take a long-distance bus such as Victory Liner to Baguio. It usually takes
5–6 hours
. A regular air-conditioned bus used to cost about ₱445, and it has since gone up, so check the current fare locally.
There is no direct flight from Manila (MNL) to Baguio, so go overland.
Direct buses from Manila to Mount Data are not common. Go via Baguio or Bontoc.
At the Dangwa Terminal or the Lizardo Terminal in Baguio, take a Sagada-bound bus such as GL Trans or Lizardo, which passes near Mount Data. The ride to Sagada takes
5–6 hours
, and many sources give a fare of about ₱220, but sources differ, so confirm locally.
Vans also run from Baguio to Bauko (Abatan). The fare was about ₱180 in 2018 and they are said to run from early morning to afternoon, but confirm the latest schedule locally.
The hotel says it is about
3 hours
by car from Baguio. A chartered van or private car lets you stop anywhere along the way.
From the GL Trans terminal in Bontoc, vans toward Pak-as run from early morning to evening, and you can continue to Abatan (from about ₱50 as of 2018).
From Banaue, go to Bontoc first and transfer there.

The dry months from November to May are the most reliable. Because you are high in the mountains, mornings and evenings are very cold even in the dry season, and clear days offer the best views of the sky and stars.

From June to October, the rainy and typhoon season brings fog, rain and a higher risk of landslides. After heavy rain Halsema Highway is repeatedly cut or reduced to one lane, so check road conditions before you set out in this period.

The most dependable place to stay in the park is Mount Data Hotel. Renovated and reopened in 2022, it has 22 rooms, two 10-person dormitories, meeting rooms, a restaurant and a coffee shop. The booking page lists standard rooms from about ₱2,700, but this changes with the season and promotions, so check the official site. The dormitory is a way to cut costs.

There are few restaurants outside the hotel. It is easiest to eat at the hotel restaurant or to bring snacks from Baguio or Bontoc. In nearby Bauko and Atok there are farm stands selling vegetables and strawberries. If you want a wider choice of lodging and food, the practical option is to stay in Sagada or Baguio and visit as a day trip.
Bring warm clothing. It is cool even by day and very cold at night. Gloves and a hat are also useful.
The last bus leaves early, so start in the morning. Mount Data is in the middle of the route, so if a bus is full you may not get on.
Mobile signal is weak in places, so download your map for offline use.
Bring plenty of cash. There is no ATM nearby.
Bring motion sickness medicine. Halsema Highway has very many sharp bends.
When walking in the forest, carry out all your trash and do not touch plants or wildlife.
For treks such as the Seven Peaks, register at the barangay office and hire a local guide.
Landslides and road collapses are frequent on Halsema Highway in the rainy season, so check the latest road advisories before you leave.
In August 2024 a section of Halsema Highway collapsed in Buguias, and landslides in Atok and elsewhere have cut traffic since then.
Fog makes driving visibility very poor, so avoid driving at night.
At high altitude, watch for hypothermia and bring a raincoat so you do not get soaked.
Park fees, guide fees and schedules change often. Check the latest notices locally.
Check typhoon forecasts in the summer months.
A well-known mountain town you can reach by continuing on the bus, famous for its caves and hanging coffins. Many travelers go on to Sagada from Mount Data.
The highland city that serves as the starting point, about
3 hours
by car from Mount Data.
A town with the Halsema Highway highest-point viewpoint and vegetable and strawberry farms.
World-famous rice terraces that you can reach via Bontoc.
Luzon's second-highest peak on the Benguet side, famous for its sea of clouds.
